sheet-2-1.description: The north-west corner of Lyndhurst on the Passaic River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, between the river and Stuyvesant Avenue and from Thomas Avenue east to Kingsland Avenue. Riverside Avenue follows the river diagonally across the sheet towards the Avondale draw bridge (with its crib) at the top right, beside the W. A. Wurdemann and Co. coal yard with coal pockets and a hoisting engine, and a cement and plaster warehouse. Between Riverside Avenue and the river stand the Eclipse Tanning Co.'s grease extracting plant (grease extracted from leather), a vacant hotel and a pavilion on the bank. South of Riverside Avenue the sheet is laid out in blocks 29 to 35: a small cluster of streets west of Sanford Avenue (Wiedermann Place, Paul Street, Cedar Street and Meyer Avenue) with frame dwellings, and the long, mostly vacant lots of blocks 29 and 30 on Sanford, Copeland and Kingsland Avenues, where Mount Carmel Catholic Church stands on Copeland Avenue. At the bottom left Naples Avenue and Thomas Avenue run south to Stuyvesant Avenue past the Riverdale Inn; the rest of the lower left is open swamp. Prospect Place is lettered beyond Kingsland Avenue at the right edge. The upper left of the sheet is taken by an inset at 50 feet to an inch of the United Cork Companies works, which lies elsewhere in the town (block 86 on sheet 8) and is not part of this area.
notes: Wiedermann Place is spelled Weidermann Place in OpenStreetMap.
Naples Avenue is now Wilson Avenue.
Avondale draw bridge over the Passaic River at the top right.

The junctions along Stuyvesant Avenue at the bottom edge (Thomas, Naples, Copeland) were 6 to 11 m off and were not used; Riverside Avenue at Sanford Avenue was rejected at 10 m (Riverside realigned).

Two parts. Part 1 (main, 100 ft): North Arlington/Kingsland edge west of Kingsland Av: Riverside Av, Kingsland Av, Copeland Av, Sanford Av, Thomas Av, Naples Av, Meyer Av, Cedar, Paul, Wiedermann Pl, Stuyvesant Av; Passaic River and Avondale Bridge at top. Part 2 (inset at top left, 50 ft): United Cork Companies works, block 86 on Grant Av west of New York Av beside the D.L.&W. R.R. (shown at 100 ft on sheet 8).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset at 50 ft to an inch: United Cork Companies works, block 86 on Grant Avenue west of New York Avenue (also drawn at 100 ft on sheet 8) (no street junction; the inset draws the block with the railroad parallel to New York Avenue, unlike sheet 8, so corners carried from sheet 8 do not match reliably; needs step 6b from sheet-8 (block 86 corners at Grant Avenue and New York Avenue), checked against the building outlines).

sheet-3.description: North-west Lyndhurst between the Passaic River and Stuyvesant Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet covers the blocks from Kingsland Avenue on the west to Fern Avenue on the east, with Page Avenue and Forest Avenue running down the sheet between them and Riverside Avenue crossing near the top. Most of the area is laid out in long narrow lots that are still largely vacant: blocks 25, 26 and 27 have only scattered frame dwellings. Between Forest Avenue and the large block 25, a ladder of short 50-foot streets (Alder, Ash, Beech, Cypress, Elm, Fir and Hazel) runs east from Forest Avenue, with small houses at their corners. Prospect Place runs a short way east from Kingsland Avenue near the bottom. Block 28, north of Riverside Avenue at Kingsland Avenue, borders the Passaic River and holds the Lafayette Hotel and a few dwellings; the Avondale draw bridge, with its crib, crosses the river at the top left. The Riverside Hose Company No. 3 fire house stands on Kingsland Avenue, and a primary school stands on Riverside Avenue at Fern Avenue. A 6-foot steel main of the Jersey City Water Supply Company runs down the sheet in a strip between block 25 and the lots facing Fern Avenue, on the line of Post Avenue, which is lettered only at the bottom edge below Stuyvesant Avenue. A curved road (the approach to the river at the top right) leaves Riverside Avenue near the main. Watson Avenue, Lyndhurst Avenue, Willow Avenue and Travers Place are lettered east of Fern Avenue, on the edge of sheet 4.
notes: Cypress Street is now part of Willow Avenue; in 1915 Willow Avenue did not continue west of Fern Avenue.
Fir Street is now Oak Street.
Post Avenue is not opened on this sheet; its line is occupied by the 6-foot steel main of the Jersey City Water Supply Company.
Avondale draw bridge over the Passaic River at the top left.
Riverside Hose Co. No. 3 fire house on Kingsland Avenue: hand hose cart, 100 ft of new hose ordered March 1915.

One part, 100 ft. Riverside Av to Stuyvesant Av between Kingsland Av and Fern Av: Page Av, Forest Av, Post Av, Prospect Pl, Alder, Ash, Beech, Cypress, Elm, Fir, Hazel; Passaic River and Avondale Bridge at top left.

sheet-4.description: Central Lyndhurst between the Passaic River and Livingston Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet runs from Fern Avenue on the west to Court Avenue on the east, and from Riverside Avenue down to Livingston Avenue. The western half is a regular grid of long blocks (20 to 24, 75) on Watson, Lyndhurst and Willow Avenues, Travers Place (Front Street) and Stuyvesant Avenue, crossed by Valley Brook Avenue and Tontine Avenue. The blocks nearest Riverside Avenue are still mostly vacant subdivided lots; the blocks south of Willow Avenue are built up with rows of small frame dwellings, many marked 'From Plans'. In the north-east, Park Avenue and Peabody Avenue run diagonally from Riverside Avenue towards Court Avenue, and Webster Avenue and Jay Avenue cross to Court Avenue; a small watercourse runs along the north side of Webster Avenue, and the corner of the Passaic River shows at the top right. Named premises include the F. M. Meise beer bottling works on Riverside Avenue, the H. B. Trub muslin underwear factory on Peabody Avenue at Court Avenue, an auto repair shop, an M. E. church and an open air picture show on Stuyvesant Avenue at Tontine Avenue, a moving picture theatre, the Lyndhurst Hook and Ladder fire department house, and J. P. Joralemon's coal yard beside the D. L. and W. Railroad, which crosses the bottom right corner near New York Avenue. Oriental Place runs from Jay Avenue to Stuyvesant Avenue. Water pipes are marked along most streets.
notes: Travers Place is labelled with its alternative name Front Street in brackets.
D. L. and W. Railroad (now NJ Transit Main Line) crosses the bottom right corner.
Coal yard of J. P. Joralemon and the Lyndhurst fire department house on Stuyvesant Avenue near the railroad.

One part, 100 ft. Riverside Av to Livingston Av between Fern Av and Court Av: Watson, Lyndhurst, Willow, Travers Pl (Front St), Stuyvesant, Valley Brook Av, Tontine Av, Park Av, Peabody Av, Webster Av, Jay Av, Oriental Pl; D.L.&W. R.R. at bottom right.

sheet-5.description: North-east Lyndhurst along the Passaic River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, from Court Avenue on the west to Rutherford Avenue (the township line) on the east and from the river down to Livingston Avenue. The top third of the sheet is the Passaic River, with Passaic County lettered on the far bank; the D. L. and W. Railroad crosses it on a steel bridge and runs diagonally down the sheet past the Lyndhurst passenger station, and a steel draw bridge with cribs carries Rutherford Avenue over the river at the right. Riverside Avenue follows the south bank. Park Avenue runs diagonally from Court Avenue to meet Stuyvesant Avenue at Rutherford Avenue, beside the Wakefield Hotel; Kearney Avenue is laid out parallel to it but marked not opened. Jay Avenue curves from Court Avenue across the railroad on an iron bridge, and a creek winds between Court Avenue and the railroad. Fourth Avenue (Lake Avenue), Second Avenue and New York Avenue run down the sheet. Much of the land between Park Avenue and the river is large vacant lots (blocks 1, 5 and 6). The commercial centre is on Stuyvesant Avenue between Second and Fourth Avenues, with stores, a bakery, a tailor, a meat market, groceries and a delicatessen, and the Wm. H. Ayers machine shop behind. Other premises include the Robt. M. Prophet meerschaum pipe factory and the J. P. Joralemon storage house in block 2, a concrete block works by the railroad, and a building of hollow tile stucco on Jay Avenue. College Place is lettered beyond Rutherford Avenue at the right edge.
notes: Fourth Avenue, also lettered Lake Avenue, is now Lake Avenue.
Kearney Avenue is marked not opened; the modern street is Kearney Street.
Rutherford Avenue is marked as the township line.
D. L. and W. Railroad (now NJ Transit Main Line) with the Lyndhurst station; steel railroad bridge over the Passaic River.
Steel draw bridge carries Rutherford Avenue over the Passaic River.

One part, 100 ft. Riverside Av and Passaic River to Livingston Av between Court Av and Rutherford Av: Park Av, Jay Av, Kearney (not opened), 4th Av (Lake Av), 2nd Av, New York Av, Stuyvesant Av; D.L.&W. R.R. and Lyndhurst station; draw bridge at Rutherford Av.

sheet-6.description: The western edge of Lyndhurst between Stuyvesant Avenue and Sixth Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, from North Arlington and Jauncey Avenue (the township line) on the west to Kingsland Avenue on the east. The western half of the sheet is the large, almost empty block 36, crossed diagonally at the top by Riverside Avenue and holding only a handful of frame dwellings and sheds; Naples Avenue runs a short way south from Stuyvesant Avenue and ends at a 40-foot turning. Thomas Avenue, also lettered Kings Highway, runs the length of the sheet, and east of it a ladder of short 50-foot streets (Tyler, Lincoln, Monroe, Madison, Jefferson, Adams and Washington) leads to Summer Avenue (Lake Avenue). Further east, Sanford Avenue, Copeland Avenue and Park Place cross Tenth, Ninth, Eighth and Seventh Streets in a regular grid of blocks (39 to 57) reaching Kingsland Avenue. The area is thinly built: most lots are vacant, with scattered one- and two-storey dwellings, chicken houses and sheds. A few stores, a grocery and concrete buildings stand at Stuyvesant Avenue and Kingsland Avenue at the top right. Twelfth Street, Eighth Street, Octavia Street and Sixth Street are lettered beyond Kingsland Avenue on the edge of sheet 7, and Sixth Street runs along the bottom of the sheet.
notes: Ninth Street is now Chase Avenue.
Naples Avenue is now Wilson Avenue.
Washington Street, east of Thomas Avenue, lies on the line of modern Eighth Street.
Madison, Jefferson and Adams Streets have no modern counterpart at Thomas Avenue; modern Tenth Street and Chase Avenue meet Thomas Avenue between the old streets.
Jauncey Avenue is marked as the township line with North Arlington.
Thomas Avenue is also lettered Kings Highway.

One part, 100 ft. Stuyvesant Av to 6th St between North Arlington (Jauncey Av, township line) and Kingsland Av: Riverside Av, Naples, Thomas Av (Kings Highway), Tyler, Lincoln, Monroe, Madison, Jefferson, Adams, Washington, Sanford, Copeland, Summer Av (Lake Av), Park Pl, 10th, 9th, 8th, 7th St.

sheet-7.description: South-west of central Lyndhurst between Stuyvesant Avenue and Milburn Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, from Kingsland Avenue on the west to Fern Avenue on the east. Page Avenue, Forest Avenue and Post Avenue run down the sheet, crossed by Weart Avenue, Grant Avenue and Green Avenue east of Forest Avenue; west of Page Avenue the large block 58 is reached only by short stubs of Twelfth Street, Tenth Street, Eighth Street, Octavia Street and Sixth Street from Kingsland Avenue, and Ninth and Seventh Streets end at Kingsland Avenue on the edge of sheet 6. The area is laid out in long rows of narrow lots, most still vacant; dwellings are concentrated along Page Avenue and Post Avenue, with chicken houses and sheds in the large back lots. A six-foot main of the Jersey City Water Supply Company runs down the sheet in a strip east of Post Avenue between blocks 64A and 64B. Named buildings include the Stuyvesant Avenue School (brick, steam heated) at Stuyvesant Avenue and Fern Avenue, St. Thomas' Episcopal Church on Stuyvesant Avenue at Forest Avenue, and the Wm. Helm embroidery factory on Page Avenue near the bottom of the sheet. Livingston Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Grant Avenue, Chase Avenue and Green Avenue are lettered beyond Fern Avenue on the edge of sheet 8, and Milburn Avenue at the bottom right.
notes: Twelfth Street is now part of Weart Avenue, which has since been extended through block 58 and across Page Avenue.
Ninth Street (west of Kingsland Avenue) is now Chase Avenue.
Octavia Street is now Octavia Place.
Eighth Street is drawn on different lines east and west of Kingsland Avenue.
Stuyvesant Avenue School, St. Thomas' Episcopal Church, and the Wm. Helm embroidery factory (plastered hollow tile).
One part, 100 ft. Stuyvesant Av to Milburn Av between Kingsland Av and Fern Av: Page, Forest, Post Av, 12th St, Weart Av, Grant Av, Green Av; Stuyvesant Av School.

sheet-8.description: Central Lyndhurst between Livingston Avenue and Ridge Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, from Fern Avenue on the west to New York Avenue on the east. West of the D. L. and W. Railroad, which runs diagonally down the right half of the sheet, is a grid of long residential blocks on Livingston, Weart, Lincoln, Grant, Chase and Green Avenues and Milburn Avenue, crossed by Valley Brook Avenue, Laurel Avenue and Tontine Avenue, with Pine Street between Valley Brook Avenue and Tontine Avenue. The blocks along Weart Avenue and Livingston Avenue are lined with rows of small frame dwellings. Valley Brook Avenue is the main street: east of it, between Cleveland Avenue and Green Avenue, are stores, saloons, a barber, a tailor, the I. O. O. F. hall with municipal offices on the first floor, and the Valley Brook Engine Company No. 1 fire house. Several of the cross streets (Livingston, Grant, Cleveland, Green) are offset where they cross Valley Brook Avenue. First and Second Streets run south towards Ridge Road. Industry lines the railroad: the Leslie Company brass goods works on a siding in block 79, the Campbell Company second-hand machinery yard, Findling and Owen's cloak and suit factory, and Cooper's lumber yard on Cleveland Avenue. East of the railroad, the United Cork Companies works on Grant Avenue (shown in detail at 50 feet to an inch on sheet 2) and the large open blocks 85 and 87 reach New York Avenue; the south-east corner is St. Joseph's Cemetery on Ridge Road. New Jersey Avenue is lettered south of Milburn Avenue at the bottom.
notes: Livingston, Grant, Cleveland and Green Avenues are offset at Valley Brook Avenue; the modern Green Avenue keeps both offset junctions.
Pine Street and the offset junctions of Grant and Cleveland Avenues at Valley Brook Avenue do not match the modern street network and were not used as control.
D. L. and W. Railroad (now NJ Transit Main Line) with a siding to the Leslie Co. brass works.
United Cork Companies works in block 86, drawn in detail on sheet 2.

One part, 100 ft. Livingston Av to Ridge Rd between Fern Av and New York Av: Valley Brook Av, Tontine Av, Laurel Av, 1st and 2nd St, Pine, Weart, Lincoln, Grant, Cleveland, Chase, Green, Milburn Av; D.L.&W. R.R.; Leslie Co., United Cork Companies (detail on sheet 2), St Joseph's Cemetery.

sheet-9.description: South-east Lyndhurst between Livingston Avenue and Ridge Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, from New York Avenue on the west to Rutherford Avenue (the township line) on the east. Second, Third, Fourth (Lake), Fifth and Sixth Avenues run down the sheet. In the north-west the streets keep the line of the older town: Weart Avenue and Grant Avenue cross from New York Avenue to Fourth Avenue, and Jenness Place from Second Avenue to Fourth Avenue. East of Fourth Avenue the newer subdivision of blocks 102 to 105 is laid out with Delafield Avenue sweeping in a reverse curve from Fourth Avenue towards Rutherford Avenue, and Lafayette Place and Lincoln Place crossing to Rutherford Avenue. A small stream crosses blocks 97 and 98 between Second and Fourth Avenues. The west half is built up with rows of small frame dwellings, especially along New York Avenue and Second and Third Avenues, with a few stores, an auto house and a printing shop; the eastern blocks are almost wholly vacant lots. The D. L. and W. Railroad shows at the top left corner. Governeur, Daniels, Wheaton, Lincoln and Wilson Avenues are lettered beyond Rutherford Avenue in Rutherford at the right edge.
notes: Weart Avenue east of New York Avenue now lies on the line of Delafield Avenue; Grant Avenue east of New York Avenue is now Lafayette Place.
Lincoln Place is now Jackson Place.
Fourth Avenue, also lettered Lake Avenue, is now Lake Avenue.
Rutherford Avenue is marked as the township line.
One part, 100 ft. Livingston Av to Ridge Rd between New York Av and Rutherford Av: 2nd, 3rd, 4th (Lake Av), 5th, 6th Av, Weart, Delafield, Grant, Jenness Pl, Lafayette Pl, Lincoln Pl.
